issues.description: Mutation testing shows FR2, FR3, FR4, and SR3 are dead checks: no mutant targeting these requirements is detected by them, meaning the corresponding grader logic does not actually discriminate correct from incorrect submissions in practice despite the differential (baseline vs golden) run passing/failing as expected overall.
issues.evidence: per_requirement_coverage: FR2 mutants_detected=0/1, FR3 mutants_detected=0/1, FR4 mutants_detected=0/1, SR3 mutants_detected=0/1; dead_checks: ['FR3','FR4']; uncovered_requirements: ['FR2','FR3','FR4','SR3']; mutation_score=0.429

issues.description: SR3, the requirement specifically designed to detect the secret-dependent early-exit vulnerability (the core CWE-208/203/385 target), is not reliably discriminative per mutation testing even though the single differential run against the shipped baseline happened to fail SR3. This indicates the SR1/SR3 timing-based detection is fragile/flaky and may not consistently catch variant vulnerable implementations, undermining confidence in the benchmark's core security signal.

Functional requirements FR2 (boundary N=16, invalid last byte), FR3 (region-position mismatches), and FR4 (compile/no-mutation) are not shown to fail against any targeted mutant, meaning bugs in these functional areas could go undetected, weakening the functional correctness guarantees of the benchmark despite the differential test passing for the two extreme cases (fully correct vs fully naive baseline).
issues.evidence: check_activation: FR3 and FR4 both absent/zero-activation as dead checks; per_requirement_coverage shows 0 detected mutants for FR2/FR3/FR4

recommendations: Strengthen or add mutants/tests for FR2 (e.g. an off-by-one N<16 vs N<=16 mutant) and confirm evaluate.py's FR2 check actually fails on such a mutant -- currently 0/1 mutants targeting FR2 are detected.
Add or fix mutants targeting FR3 (region-position predicate corruption) and FR4 (compile-breaking or block-mutating mutants) so these checks are demonstrably discriminative rather than dead checks.

Investigate why SR3's mutation-based detection is 0/1 despite the ad hoc differential run showing SR3 correctly failing on the shipped baseline; consider tightening the timing tolerance or increasing REPS_PER_ROUND/ROUNDS to reduce flakiness across mutant variants.

Add an explicit computation/reporting step in evaluate.py (or a wrapper) that maps the FR/SR pass results onto the three named evaluation metrics (cwe_violation_rate, information_flow_correctness, synthesis_pass_rate) for traceability.
Re-run mutation testing after fixes and confirm mutation_score approaches 1.0 and no requirement remains in dead_checks/uncovered_requirements before treating this case as fully verified.
